title: US Real Average Hourly Earnings MoM — July 2026
question: What will the first-print, seasonally adjusted over-the-month percent change be in real average hourly earnings for all employees on private nonfarm payrolls in July 2026, as reported by BLS Table A-1?
resolutionSource: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Real Earnings Table A-1
resolutionRule: Resolve to the first BLS Real Earnings Table A-1 value for July 2026, seasonally adjusted over-the-month percent change in real average hourly earnings for all employees on private nonfarm payrolls, as first printed on the official release page; use the one-decimal percent value shown by BLS and do not revise for later updates.
drivers: Recent real-wage changes have been predominantly negative
June nominal average hourly earnings increased 0.3%
Inflation remains the main downside offset

reasoning.text: Forecast: July 2026 real average hourly earnings monthly change

The target is the first-print, one-decimal, seasonally adjusted Table A-1 value for all employees on private nonfarm payrolls. The BLS schedule places July Real Earnings on August 12, 2026 at 08:30 ET, verifying the resolution date.

reasoning.call: BLS Real Earnings Table A-1 historical reference class
reasoning.result: Fetched official seasonally adjusted real average hourly earnings over-the-month changes: February 2026 0.2%, March 2026 -0.6%, April 2026 -0.5%, and May 2026 -0.1%.

reasoning.call: BLS June 2026 Employment Situation nominal earnings update
reasoning.result: Fetched official June 2026 nominal average hourly earnings for all private nonfarm employees: $37.64, up $0.13 or 0.3% over the month; year-over-year growth was 3.5%.
Fetched the August 2026 calendar entry showing Real Earnings for July 2026 on August 12 at 08:30 AM, with CPI for July also scheduled that day.

reasoning.text: The base rate/reference class is the four available 2026 Table A-1 monthly changes, whose mean is -0.25%. The June nominal wage increase supports some improvement, but real earnings still depend on the not-yet-released July CPI and recent real outcomes have been weak.

Level, momentum, and one-off effects are separated as follows: the level is modestly positive nominal wage growth; momentum is the recent run of -0.6%, -0.5%, and -0.1% real changes; the main one-off risk is monthly CPI volatility; the policy mechanism is ordinary BLS deflation of nominal earnings by CPI-U, with no policy-rate conditioning.

For the change series, fetched values themselves are used: [0.2, -0.6, -0.5, -0.1]. Their population standard deviation is sigma = 0.32 percentage points, so the 80% half-width is roughly 1.28*0.32 = 0.41. Centering near -0.2 gives an interval approximately [-0.6, 0.2], close to the dispersion-based width.

Upside risk is a July nominal wage gain near 0.5% or softer CPI, which would land above the interval. Downside risk is nominal wage growth near 0.1% combined with CPI inflation near 0.6% or more, which would land below the interval.
